title: 3 Kitchen Essentials That Earn Their Counter Space
excerpt: An Instant Pot, a cast iron skillet and a salad spinner — the trio we'd buy first for a new kitchen.

body.p: Most kitchen gadgets end up in a drawer. These three get used every week, and with basic care they last for years.

It turns dried beans into dinner in under an hour, makes rice without a separate cooker and slow-cooks chili while you're at work. The 6-quart size is right for most families. Start with pressure-cooked chicken thighs or steel-cut oats, and it soon becomes part of your routine.

Cast iron holds heat like nothing else, which means a better sear, crispier potatoes and cornbread with real edges. It comes pre-seasoned, and every time you cook with oil the surface gets slicker. The silicone handle holder in this bundle saves your hands.
Wet greens make watery salads and soggy dressings. The OXO's pump-and-brake design dries a whole head of lettuce in seconds, and the bowl is nice enough to serve from.

ul: Rinse with hot water and scrub with a brush. A drop of soap is fine.
Dry it on the stove over low heat so it can't rust.
Wipe on a very thin layer of oil while it's still warm.
